reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a real inner-product space with any given MeasurableSpace structure. For every real kappa and every pair of measures mu,nu on phase space S=E x E,define
  P_kappa(mu,nu)=inf_{pi coupling of mu,nu} integral^- C_kappa(s,sprime) dpi(s,sprime),
where coupling means a measure on S x S whose first marginal is mu and second marginal is nu,and C_kappa(s,sprime)=ENNReal.ofReal(Q_kappa(s-sprime)) with
  Q_kappa(x,p)=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2.
This is precisely the approved transportCost call defining phaseWassersteinSq. It is an extended-nonnegative unrooted cost,storing the square rather than taking a square root. mu,nu are arbitrary measures,not assumed probability measures or finite-moment measures. kappa is unrestricted. The definition asserts no existence or attainment of a coupling and no finiteness or metric theorem.
objects: Real-inner-product E with measurable structure;real kappa;phase measures mu,nu;cost C_kappa from explicit Q;all coupling measures with the prescribed two marginals;lower-integral transport infimum P_kappa,denoting phaseWassersteinSq.
domains: E has real-inner-product and MeasurableSpace structures. kappa in R;mu,nu are Measure(E x E). Couplings lie on (E x E) x (E x E). Cost and P_kappa take values in ENNReal. No BorelSpace,second-countability,finite-dimensionality or probability assumption is stated for this definition.
quantifiers: Definition for every such E,real kappa,and measures mu,nu. It takes an infimum over all couplings,not a choice of one witnessed coupling. No finite value or kappa>=1 premise occurs.
assumptions: Only stated space structures and arbitrary measure inputs. The cost is ofReal of the explicit Q of coordinate differences. No probability normalization,equal-mass premise,finite moments or coupling certificate is provided.
conclusion: The assigned value is transportCost(C_kappa,mu,nu),namely the infimum of cost lower integrals over all couplings. The result is unrooted ENNReal cost.
scopes: This is a definition,not a metric/comparison theorem. Measures may be arbitrary and the value may be infinite. No square root,probability normalization,optimal-coupling attainment,integrability or sampler-history statement is added. No material definition ambiguity is present.
constant_dependencies: The sole parameter is kappa through Q=(1/(2kappa)+1/2)||x||^2+<x,p>+||p||^2. Cost is exactly ofReal(Q of difference);no additional multiplicative constant or root is present.
